body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and publish to npm yourself or [setup this action to publish automatically](https://github.com/changesets/action#with-publishing). If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## @objectstack/cli@18.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 42d9fe8: feat(spec,cli,lint): a form section entry's `label`, `placeholder` and `helpText` are translatable at `objects.<object>._sections.<section>.fields.<field>`
  
  Clause-②: yes (widening)
  Metadata-protocol: added
  
  A form section entry (`{ field, label, placeholder, helpText }` in a form view's `sections[].fields`) can override the object field's copy for that form. Before this change a translation pack had no key for those three strings, so a form's entry overrides stayed in the authoring language for every reader, the anonymous `GET /forms/:slug` visitor included.
  
  - **`@objectstack/spec`:** the `_sections.<section>` node of an object translation gains `fields`, keyed by the entry's `field`, each carrying `label`, `placeholder` and `helpText` (strict; `help`, `hint` and `tooltip` are refused with the rename to `helpText`). `translateView` overlays them onto a served form view's `config.sections[].fields[]` under the section rules: the key is the section's `name` and the entry's `field`, only copy the entry authors is translated, a missing key keeps the authored string, and a string edited on top of the packaged view keeps the edit (ADR-0029 D9.2a). An entry in a section with no `name`, and a bare field-name entry, have no key.
  - **`@objectstack/cli`:** `os i18n extract` scaffolds the key for every entry string a form view's named section authors, and `os i18n check` / `os lint` coverage report a locale that leaves one untranslated, in the `section` bucket.
  - **`@objectstack/lint`:** `translation-target-unknown` reports a `_sections.<section>.fields.<field>` key that no form view section of that name declares as an entry object.
  
  Example (`zh-CN` bundle):
  
  ```ts
  objects: {
    crm_case: {
      _sections: {
        submitter: {
          label: '关于您',
          fields: { contact_name: { label: '您的姓名', placeholder: '张三', helpText: '与证件一致' } },
        },
      },
    },
  }
  ```

## @objectstack/lint@18.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 42d9fe8: feat(spec,cli,lint): a form section entry's `label`, `placeholder` and `helpText` are translatable at `objects.<object>._sections.<section>.fields.<field>`
  
  Clause-②: yes (widening)
  Metadata-protocol: added
  
  A form section entry (`{ field, label, placeholder, helpText }` in a form view's `sections[].fields`) can override the object field's copy for that form. Before this change a translation pack had no key for those three strings, so a form's entry overrides stayed in the authoring language for every reader, the anonymous `GET /forms/:slug` visitor included.
  
  - **`@objectstack/spec`:** the `_sections.<section>` node of an object translation gains `fields`, keyed by the entry's `field`, each carrying `label`, `placeholder` and `helpText` (strict; `help`, `hint` and `tooltip` are refused with the rename to `helpText`). `translateView` overlays them onto a served form view's `config.sections[].fields[]` under the section rules: the key is the section's `name` and the entry's `field`, only copy the entry authors is translated, a missing key keeps the authored string, and a string edited on top of the packaged view keeps the edit (ADR-0029 D9.2a). An entry in a section with no `name`, and a bare field-name entry, have no key.
  - **`@objectstack/cli`:** `os i18n extract` scaffolds the key for every entry string a form view's named section authors, and `os i18n check` / `os lint` coverage report a locale that leaves one untranslated, in the `section` bucket.
  - **`@objectstack/lint`:** `translation-target-unknown` reports a `_sections.<section>.fields.<field>` key that no form view section of that name declares as an entry object.
  
  Example (`zh-CN` bundle):
  
  ```ts
  objects: {
    crm_case: {
      _sections: {
        submitter: {
          label: '关于您',
          fields: { contact_name: { label: '您的姓名', placeholder: '张三', helpText: '与证件一致' } },
        },
      },
    },
  }
  ```
- cc10e74: feat: a package's action can launch a flow, and its dashboard widget can bind a dataset, that another package of the same release artifact ships
  
  Clause-②: yes (widening)
  Metadata-protocol: added
  
  One release artifact carries several packages (ADR-0130 D4). Two per-package checks judged a reference against one package and refused a target a sibling package provides. The artifact carries the target, and the runtime serves it.
  
  - **`@objectstack/spec`: `defineStack(config, { artifactFlows })`.** This new `DefineStackOptions` key lists flow names that the other packages of the artifact provide. A `type: 'flow'` action's `target` resolves against the stack's own `flows` plus these names. That covers a top-level action, an action authored on an object, and an inline page action. It works the way `artifactObjects` already does for permission grants and seed rows.
    - The option widens a check that already runs. A stack that declares no flows of its own still leaves its flow targets unresolved (a plugin may serve them).
    - `defineStack` records every target that resolved only through the list, as a non-enumerable mark on the stack it returns. `composeStacks` refuses the composition when no input defines that flow. The refusal uses the same `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` envelope and the same per-finding message as the per-stack pass. An input that did not opt in cannot newly fail at composition.
    - A flow that no package of the artifact defines is refused, as before.
  - **`@objectstack/lint`: `widget-dataset-unknown`.** The rule resolves a widget's `dataset` against the datasets that every `packages[]` body declares, as well as the stack's own. This is the resolution context that `os build`, `os validate` and `os lint` already pass to each package's run. Dataset-level checks still judge only the package's own datasets. A dataset that no package declares is refused, as before. The runtime publish gate passes no `packages[]`, so its behaviour is unchanged.
  
  Fix for a module split such as HotCRM's: in the app package, write `defineStack(appConfig, { artifactFlows: revenue.flows?.map((f) => f.name) })` and compose both packages with `composeStacks([...], { manifest: 'preserve' })`. A cross-package dataset binding needs no change.

- 2af790f: spec(ui): `record:details` section `hideEmpty: false` — in read-only mode an all-empty section renders its heading plus one fold row, and the `describe()` text says so
  
  Clause-②: no
  Metadata-protocol: semantic
  
  The meaning of `hideEmpty: false` on a `record:details` section changes for a section whose fields are ALL empty (for example on a brand-new record):
  
  - **Read-only mode:** the section renders its heading plus one fold row that counts the empty fields and reveals them on request — the same fold a partly-filled section already uses. It no longer renders a column of empty rows.
  - **Edit mode:** unchanged. Every field renders as an editable row.
  
  Nothing else changes. No key is added, removed or renamed; the shape and the default are the same. Leaving `hideEmpty` out (or writing `true`) still means an all-empty section renders nothing at all: no heading, no skeleton. A partly-filled section's empty rows are not governed by this key, in either value. Authored metadata needs no change: a section that writes `hideEmpty: false` to keep its heading on an empty record keeps it.
  
  The `describe()` text, which the reference docs and the JSON Schema read, now states this. Its lead changes from "Hide this section's empty fields" to "Whether this section disappears when ALL its fields are empty", because under the new reading both values hide an all-empty section's empty rows in read-only mode and the old lead no longer told them apart. The renderer change is in objectui's record detail section.

## @objectstack/metadata-protocol@18.2.0

### Patch Changes

- f1d6be0: fix(service-analytics)!: an analytics read gate that could not decide answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, not the `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` of a real denial
  
  Three of the analytics door's refusals are operator-side faults: the object-level read admission provider threw, the field-level read permissions could not be resolved, or the API exposure declaration could not be read. Each refused the query, which is right, but each answered with the same body as a real denial, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. A caller could not tell "you may not read this" from "the server could not decide", except by parsing the English message. All three now answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. That is an existing ADR-0112 code, and it is the spelling `@objectstack/core` already uses when the permission store is unreachable. The refusal names the object and nothing else; it names no gate, grant or existence fact. The cause stays in the server log, as before. Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing that was refused is now admitted. Real denials keep their answers byte for byte: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` when the caller holds no read grant or reads a hidden field, and `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` for an unexposed object. `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` relays the declared fault as `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, with the message withheld as for every declared server fault. It does not answer `500 ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED`. The cube query door relays the status the same way.
  
  The publish build probe (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) reads the code too. A widget query that fails with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` now gets a `widget_query_failed` fix that names the server-side fault: the dataset is not the cause, and the server could not decide read access to the named object. Before, it fell to "Fix the dataset definition…", which is wrong for an outage. The finding's `code`, `severity` and `message` are unchanged.
  
  Clause-②: no
  Metadata-protocol: none
  
  <!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) No metadata moves: no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition, stored shape or exported declaration is added, removed, renamed or narrowed, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. What changes is the code and status three analytics refusals answer when a permission or exposure resolver fails (403 PERMISSION_DENIED to 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE); every request that was refused is still refused and every request that was served is still served. The remedy is on the consumer's side, reading the code, never a rewrite of a package source or a stored row. The other categories are closed on facts: both packages publish (not unpublished); no ADR-0087 id is named or touched (not registered or already-registered); and nothing exported is removed or narrowed (not runtime-interface-only, type-surface-only or runtime-export-retired). -->
  
  **BREAKING** (the wire answer of three fault refusals changes; no request that was served is refused and none that was refused is served), shipped as `patch` because the metadata protocol does not move.
  
  - **Before:** when the analytics read-admission provider threw, or the field-level read permissions or the API exposure declaration could not be resolved, the query was refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. That was the same code and status as a caller who genuinely may not read the object.
  - **Now:** the same refusals answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`status: 503`, `object` naming the object). On `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` the body is `{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE","error":"Internal server error"}`. Real denials still answer `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (and `404` / `405` for exposure), unchanged.
  - **Fix:** a client that treated every analytics `403` as "no access" should treat `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as a server-side fault: retry once the permission or exposure resolver is healthy, and check the server log for the cause. Do not show it as a missing grant.

- 2351c8d: fix(plugin-approvals): an SLA escalation that reassigns to a target resolving to no one keeps the request on its approvers and notifies them, instead of stranding it on a slate nobody can decide

  An approval node's `escalation: { action: 'reassign', escalateTo }` expands `escalateTo` to the holders of that position, and when nobody holds it falls back to the value itself, so a config naming a specific user id keeps working. That fallback is now judged by the same rule the reassign door applies: a user id or email an account carries (and not a user of other organizations only), or `position:<name>` for a position someone in the request's organization holds.

  - **A target that does not** (an unstaffed or mistyped position name, a user id with no account, a `team:` / `department:` / `org_membership_level:` / `role:` literal) no longer replaces the slate. The pending approvers are kept and receive `approval.sla_breached`, and the `escalate` audit row records `reassign → <target> — not applied: <why>`. The escalation still fires once.
  - **The submitter's escalation notice** now names the action actually taken (`notify` when the reassign was not applied, or when no `escalateTo` was set), not the configured one.
  - A directory read that fails during the sweep leaves the request untouched and unmarked, so the next sweep retries it.
  
  Nothing an author writes is refused that was accepted before. To have an overdue request move, name a staffed position or a person in the request's organization in `escalateTo`.

### Patch Changes

- e8de8a7: Clause-②: no
  Metadata-protocol: none
  
  A new organization now gets its default currency from its creator's language or region. When an organization is created through `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/create`, the server reads the creator's stored language (`sys_user.locale`), or else the creating request's `Accept-Language`. It writes that region's ISO 4217 currency as the organization's `localization.currency`: `zh-CN` gives `CNY`, `ja` gives `JPY`, `en-GB` gives `GBP`. The value is an ordinary tenant setting, so Setup → Localization shows it and can change it. Amounts in `currencyMode: 'dynamic'` fields then show that currency instead of a plain number.
  
  When there is nothing to derive from (no stored language, no `Accept-Language`, or a tag with no country such as `es-419`), nothing is written and the setting stays unset, as before. There is no fallback to the `default_country` or `locale` platform defaults. A value already set on any rung (the organization's own, a global row, or an `OS_LOCALIZATION_CURRENCY` override) is never overwritten. A host's own `onOrganizationCreated` callback still runs, before this step.
  
  The `os dev` seed does the same for its admin's workspace from the host's POSIX locale (`LC_ALL`, then `LC_MONETARY`, then `LANG`), beside its time-zone seeding. `C`, `POSIX`, and a host with no locale set write nothing.
  
  The region-to-currency table is a checked-in snapshot of CLDR 48 `currencyData`.

### Patch Changes

- 50af6fa: fix(rest)!: an inline import mapping entry's `transform`, `defaultValue` and `required` are applied, not dropped
  
  `POST /api/v1/data/:object/import`, the async import job and plugin-auth's admin user import (`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/import-users`) all parse their body through the same request parser, which accepts `mapping` as a `FieldMappingEntry[]`, whose entries carry `transform`, `defaultValue` and `required`. The request parser kept only the column each entry names with `sourceField` and the field it names with `targetField` and dropped the rest, so a request asking for `transform: 'uppercase'` validated, ran, and stored the cell unchanged. Each entry's rules now run on its column before the cells are coerced:
  
  - `trim`, `uppercase` and `lowercase` rewrite a string cell. `none` and `lookup` copy it; a `lookup` cell is resolved to a record id by the import's reference resolution, as before.
  - `defaultValue` fills a cell that is blank (absent, empty, whitespace or one of the request's `nullValues`).
  - `required: true` refuses the request with `400 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` when a row still leaves that column blank, naming the column and the rows. The refusal comes before any row is written, on the dry run and the commit alike.
  - `transform: 'date_format'` refuses the request with `400 UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM`: an entry carries no date format for it to apply. A cell mapped to a date or datetime field is already parsed as a date, so drop the transform. A transform name outside the declared set is refused the same way.
  
  A plain `{ sourceField, targetField }` entry, and the compact `{ column: field }` record, map columns exactly as before.
  
  Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the import doors (the sync import, the async import job and plugin-auth's admin user import) refuse two request shapes they used to run: an inline mapping entry declaring `transform: 'date_format'` (or a transform name outside the declared set), and an entry marked `required: true` whose column a row leaves blank. Nothing is widened.
  
  Metadata-protocol: none (a REST import request's handling; nothing a metadata author writes changes)
  
  <!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) No metadata moves: no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition, stored row or stored shape is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, and no exported declaration is removed or narrowed, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. What changes is how the REST import doors handle a request body's inline mapping entries: their declared per-cell rules now run, and two shapes those rules make unanswerable are refused. The remedy is a request edit (drop `date_format`, fill the required cells or give the entry a `defaultValue`), never a rewrite of a package source or a stored row. The other categories are closed on facts: the package publishes (not unpublished); no ADR-0087 id is named or touched (not registered or already-registered); and nothing exported is removed or narrowed (not runtime-interface-only, type-surface-only or runtime-export-retired). -->
  
  **BREAKING** for a caller that relied on either request running.
  
  - **Before.** An inline entry's `transform`, `defaultValue` and `required` were ignored; the import ran with the rename alone.
  - **Now.** They are applied; `date_format` and a blank `required` cell refuse the request with `400`.
  - **Fix.** Drop `transform: 'date_format'` from the entry (the date field's own parse still applies), and fill a required column or give its entry a `defaultValue`.

## @objectstack/service-analytics@18.2.0

### Patch Changes

- f1d6be0: fix(service-analytics)!: an analytics read gate that could not decide answers `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, not the `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` of a real denial
  
  Three of the analytics door's refusals are operator-side faults: the object-level read admission provider threw, the field-level read permissions could not be resolved, or the API exposure declaration could not be read. Each refused the query, which is right, but each answered with the same body as a real denial, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. A caller could not tell "you may not read this" from "the server could not decide", except by parsing the English message. All three now answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. That is an existing ADR-0112 code, and it is the spelling `@objectstack/core` already uses when the permission store is unreachable. The refusal names the object and nothing else; it names no gate, grant or existence fact. The cause stays in the server log, as before. Fail-closed is unchanged: nothing that was refused is now admitted. Real denials keep their answers byte for byte: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` when the caller holds no read grant or reads a hidden field, and `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` / `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` for an unexposed object. `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` relays the declared fault as `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, with the message withheld as for every declared server fault. It does not answer `500 ANALYTICS_QUERY_FAILED`. The cube query door relays the status the same way.
  
  The publish build probe (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) reads the code too. A widget query that fails with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` now gets a `widget_query_failed` fix that names the server-side fault: the dataset is not the cause, and the server could not decide read access to the named object. Before, it fell to "Fix the dataset definition…", which is wrong for an outage. The finding's `code`, `severity` and `message` are unchanged.
  
  Clause-②: no
  Metadata-protocol: none
  
  <!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) No metadata moves: no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition, stored shape or exported declaration is added, removed, renamed or narrowed, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite. What changes is the code and status three analytics refusals answer when a permission or exposure resolver fails (403 PERMISSION_DENIED to 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE); every request that was refused is still refused and every request that was served is still served. The remedy is on the consumer's side, reading the code, never a rewrite of a package source or a stored row. The other categories are closed on facts: both packages publish (not unpublished); no ADR-0087 id is named or touched (not registered or already-registered); and nothing exported is removed or narrowed (not runtime-interface-only, type-surface-only or runtime-export-retired). -->
  
  **BREAKING** (the wire answer of three fault refusals changes; no request that was served is refused and none that was refused is served), shipped as `patch` because the metadata protocol does not move.
  
  - **Before:** when the analytics read-admission provider threw, or the field-level read permissions or the API exposure declaration could not be resolved, the query was refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. That was the same code and status as a caller who genuinely may not read the object.
  - **Now:** the same refusals answer `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`status: 503`, `object` naming the object). On `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` the body is `{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE","error":"Internal server error"}`. Real denials still answer `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (and `404` / `405` for exposure), unchanged.
  - **Fix:** a client that treated every analytics `403` as "no access" should treat `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` as a server-side fault: retry once the permission or exposure resolver is healthy, and check the server log for the cause. Do not show it as a missing grant.
